design.title: Same place, same belief: each member's tile-belief map for one place must agree across the three survey photographs (Jensen-Shannon consistency, AugMix-style), trained on batches that hold every place in all three surveys
design.init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR
design.eli5: The model learns Berlin from three different aerial photographs taken in different years and seasons. Until now it was graded on each photograph separately, so it could recognise a street corner in one photo with total certainty and only half-heartedly in another, and nobody minded. Now, every time it studies a place, it sees that place in all three photographs at once and is also marked down whenever its three answers disagree — so it learns to be equally sure about a place whatever photograph it is looking at, which is what it needs when the drone's own camera shows it a fourth.
design.hypothesis: Champion exp 20 (0.0777) on held-out truedop_2024: usable 93.0%, false 0.75% (3 frames), abstain 6.25% (25 frames); the three training photographs score 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints. So what remains is purely the survey gap, and it is mostly ABSTENTION: on a foreign photograph a member's belief spreads off the right 3x3 block (min-member block mass < 0.3). The run's own clean diagnostic shows the same gap INSIDE training: on 512 fixed clean training-lattice places, each member's argmax tile agrees across the three training surveys only 84% of the time (xsurvey_agree [0.844, 0.844]) while per-survey clean top1 is ~0.88-0.91 — i.e. the loss never asks a member to hold the SAME belief about a place in two photographs; it asks each photograph separately to hit the label, and CE is satisfied by survey-specific routes to it, with survey-specific confidence. Two facts about the code make this sharper than it looks: (1) the cross-entropy cannot see agreement at all, and (2) although chunks are 'paired' (every position in all three surveys), run_epoch draws each 64-view mini-batch by a random permutation of the 4,095-view chunk, so the three survey views of a place almost never meet in one gradient step. Every earlier attempt at cross-survey invariance acted on the FEATURE (exp 3: cosine of GAP features, from scratch, reverted; exp 9: within-place variance penalty, crashed at 1e9, never measured; exp 8: DINOv2 distillation, from scratch, reverted), before the pretrained trunk existed and never on the thing the confidence gate actually reads. This experiment acts on the OUTPUT: the belief distribution over 2,970 tiles. Following AugMix (Hendrycks et al., ICLR 2020), whose Jensen-Shannon consistency across augmented views is the component that most improved accuracy AND calibration under distribution shift, each member's deployed softmax for one place in the three surveys is pulled toward their mixture. A member that already knows the place in two surveys gets a gradient telling its third view to put its belief in the same place with the same sharpness — exactly the behaviour an abstaining 2024 frame lacks. Since the photometric augmentation is drawn independently per view, the term also asks for agreement across re-photographing nuisances. Builds on exp 2 (paired-survey batches, kept) by finally making the pairing reach the gradient, and on exps 3/9 by moving their invariance goal from feature space to belief space on today's pretrained trunk. Architecture, graph, decode, committee, MixStyle, margin loss, augmentation, schedule and weight averaging all unchanged; the members stay independent (no cross-member term).
